meta.depth_rule: Every strategy that names an action is placed on a lever (L3), judged by meaning with the lever's joins_when and joins_not tests; a summary line with no action stays on its family (L2); a group alone is not a placement. A pathway (L4) is recorded only when the lever has one pathway or the strategy's wording names the channel. The pathways' text cues are an advisory flag, never a veto.

subpillars.name: Tackling Structural Exclusion
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that address the exclusion of specific groups, including women, youth, informal workers, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities, as well as the structural barriers that limit their opportunities, such as discrimination, unequal access to services and resources, limited voice and participation, and lack of protection of rights and dignity. Formalisation of informal workers belongs here, including registration, labour contracts, labour rights, and social insurance or pension coverage.

subpillars.name: Enhancing Capabilities
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that expand people's capabilities to lead healthy, productive, and resilient lives, including through education, skills, digital access, health, social protection, food security, livelihoods, and basic services. This category is intentionally broad enough to include areas that may otherwise fall under 'human security,' avoiding an artificial distinction between capability-building and protection from vulnerability.

subpillars.name: Future Generations
subpillars.definition: Covers whether today's strategies protect long-term well-being and avoid shifting risks or costs onto future generations, including through climate resilience, just transition, nature and biodiversity, sustainable resource use, intergenerational equity and responsible public finance.

subpillars.name: Export-led
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that grow the economy through external markets, including export promotion and diversification, trade agreements and market access, foreign direct investment, international tourism, trade logistics, and the innovation and technology upgrading that make traded sectors competitive.

subpillars.name: Domestic Integration
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that strengthen links within the domestic economy, including local value chains and value addition, agro-processing, industrial clusters, and connections between regions and between rural and urban markets.

subpillars.name: Growth through Inclusion
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that create jobs and incomes for groups left out of growth, including women, youth, informal workers and rural households, through enterprise development, MSME support, productivity, finance and market access. Formalisation of informal businesses belongs here, including registration, licensing, and access to finance and markets.

subpillars.name: Anticipation and Strategic Foresight
subpillars.definition: Focuses on the ability of governments to identify and prepare for future risks, opportunities and disruptions, including through horizon scanning, scenario planning, early warning, contingency planning, risk-informed analysis, and future-oriented strategy.

subpillars.name: Adaptability and Course Correction
subpillars.definition: Refers to the capacity to adjust priorities, policies, plans, and investments in response to new evidence, changing conditions or shifting development needs. This includes institutional flexibility, learning by doing, revising strategies, and making timely course corrections.

subpillars.name: Agility and Delivery Capability
subpillars.definition: Captures the ability of institutions to act quickly and effectively, mobilize resources, coordinate across government, implement reforms and respond to shocks or emerging priorities without major disruption.

subpillars.name: Reform Leadership, Coalitions and Civic Engagement
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that build the political, institutional, and social support needed to advance reform, including political will, reform incentives, collaborative leadership, coalitions, public-private collaboration, civic participation, and co-creation.

levers.evidence: Unpaid care burden and female labour supply: Goldin 1995; Clark et al. 2019
levers.intervention_evidence: Halim, Perova and Reynolds 2023, Childcare and Mothers' Labor Market Outcomes in Lower- and Middle-Income Countries, World Bank Research Observer
levers.evidence_finding: Most studies find subsidised or public childcare raises mothers' employment in low- and middle-income countries, with larger effects where care is affordable, full-day and matched to working hours.

levers.lever: Rules on hiring, dismissal and contract types
levers.lever_full: Rules on hiring, dismissal and contract types
levers.family: Exclusion from markets: labour, informality and workers' rights
levers.joins_when: it changes how costly it is to hire or dismiss workers, or what contracts are allowed
levers.joins_not: it sets wages (L3-179) or lowers the cost of being formal (L3-180)
levers.pathways: L3-178 Employment protection and hiring
levers.text_cues: labou?r (law|code|regulation|market flexib|market reform)|flexible (work|employment|labou?r)|dismissal|employment protection|severance|hiring and firing
levers.evidence: Employment protection and hiring: Besley and Burgess 2004
levers.intervention_evidence: Betcherman 2015, Labor Market Regulations: What Do We Know about Their Impacts in Developing Countries?, World Bank Research Observer
levers.evidence_finding: Stricter hiring and dismissal rules have modest effects on total employment in developing countries but shift jobs toward insiders and informality; effects are largest where rules are strictly enforced.

levers.lever: Lower taxes, simpler registration and visible benefits for formal work
levers.lever_full: Lower taxes, simpler registration and visible benefits for formal work
levers.family: Exclusion from markets: labour, informality and workers' rights
levers.joins_when: it makes formal employment or formal self-employment cheaper or more attractive
levers.joins_not: it registers firms rather than workers (L3-168) or extends insurance to informal workers (L3-260)
levers.pathways: L3-180 Informality and formalisation costs
entry_points: Tourism Employment Registration Facilitation
levers.evidence: Informality and formalisation costs: La Porta and Shleifer 2014; Ulyssea 2018
levers.intervention_evidence: Jessen and Kluve 2021, The effectiveness of interventions to reduce informality in low- and middle-income countries, World Development
levers.evidence_finding: Lower registration costs and simplified procedures alone rarely move firms into formality; combined incentives, information and stronger enforcement or inspection produce larger, though still modest, formalisation effects.

levers.lever: Collective bargaining rights, labour standards and their enforcement
levers.lever_full: Collective bargaining rights, labour standards and their enforcement
levers.family: Exclusion from markets: labour, informality and workers' rights
levers.joins_when: it strengthens workers' representation, rights or standards at work
levers.joins_not: it is only about safety inspection (L3-182) or wages (L3-179)
levers.pathways: L3-181 Worker voice and labour standards
levers.text_cues: (trade|labou?r) union|\bunions?\b|collective bargain|decent work|labou?r (right|standard)|worker.?s rights|freedom of association
levers.evidence: Worker voice and labour standards: Freeman and Medoff 1984
levers.intervention_evidence: OECD 2019, Negotiating Our Way Up: Collective Bargaining in a Changing World of Work, OECD Publishing
levers.evidence_finding: Coordinated collective bargaining is associated with higher employment, lower wage inequality and better job quality; benefits depend on coordination across bargaining levels and on coverage reaching non-standard workers.

levers.lever: Workplace safety rules and inspection
levers.lever_full: Workplace safety rules and inspection
levers.family: Exclusion from markets: labour, informality and workers' rights
levers.joins_when: it inspects or regulates safety and health at work
levers.joins_not: it is about labour rights in general (L3-181)
levers.pathways: L3-182 Workplace safety enforcement
levers.evidence: Workplace safety enforcement: Levine, Toffel and Johnson 2012
levers.intervention_evidence: Mischke et al. 2013, Occupational safety and health enforcement tools for preventing occupational diseases and injuries, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
levers.evidence_finding: Inspections may reduce injuries over the longer term, but the evidence is low quality, mostly from high-income countries, and effects are unclear for one-off or warning-only inspections.

levers.lever: Contribution rules, subsidies and enrolment channels
levers.lever_full: Contribution rules, subsidies and enrolment channels that bring informal workers into pensions and health insurance
levers.family: Exclusion from markets: labour, informality and workers' rights
levers.joins_when: it extends social insurance, pensions or health cover to workers outside formal employment
levers.joins_not: it covers the poor through assistance rather than insurance (F-06) or formalises work (L3-180)
levers.pathways: L3-260 Extension of contributory social insurance to informal workers
entry_points: Social Security System Improvement for Informal Workers
Voluntary Retirement Savings Incentives
Comprehensive Social Insurance and Welfare Service Integration
Health Security and Reimbursement Access for Undocumented Migrants and Workers
levers.evidence: Extension of contributory social insurance to informal workers: Levy 2008; ILO World Social Protection Report 2020-22 (source still to check)
levers.intervention_evidence: Banerjee, Finkelstein, Hanna, Olken, Ornaghi and Sumarto 2021, The Challenges of Universal Health Insurance in Developing Countries: Experimental Evidence from Indonesia's National Health Insurance, American Economic Review
levers.evidence_finding: Temporary premium subsidies sharply raised enrolment of informal workers in Indonesia's national health insurance, but enrolment fell when subsidies ended and attracted sicker members; information and assisted registration did little.

levers.lever: Accessible buildings, transport, information and services
levers.lever_full: Accessible buildings, transport, information and services; universal design; assistive devices
levers.joins_when: it removes physical, information or attitudinal barriers for people with disabilities or reduced mobility
levers.joins_not: it is a general service expansion with no access barrier named (the family) or anti-discrimination law (L3-001)
levers.pathways: L3-004 Disability-related access barriers
entry_points: Inclusive Learning Materials Development
Elderly-Friendly Urbanization with Universal Design
Universal and Tailor-Designed Infrastructure for Inclusive Access
Universal Design for Urban Infrastructure
Digital Welfare Services for Persons with Disabilities Development Project
levers.evidence: Disability-related access barriers: Mitra, Posarac and Vick 2013
levers.intervention_evidence: Saran, White and Kuper 2020, Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries, Campbell Systematic Reviews
levers.evidence_finding: Rigorous evaluations of accessibility measures for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries are rare; most studies concern health and rehabilitation, leaving built-environment and information access largely unevaluated.

levers.lever: Civil registration, identity documents and one-stop registration
levers.lever_full: Civil registration, identity documents and one-stop registration services
levers.joins_when: it registers people or issues the documents they need to claim services, rights or finance
levers.joins_not: it registers firms (L3-168) or builds a data system for the state (F-43)
levers.pathways: L3-006 Documentation barriers to entitlements

levers.evidence: Documentation barriers to entitlements: Dahan and Gelb 2015
levers.intervention_evidence: Muralidharan, Niehaus and Sukhtankar 2016, Building State Capacity: Evidence from Biometric Smartcards in India, American Economic Review | Muralidharan, Niehaus and Sukhtankar 2025, Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India, Review of Economics and Statistics
levers.evidence_finding: Biometric identity cut leakage and payment delays in Indian welfare payments, but making biometric verification mandatory for food rations excluded some genuine beneficiaries without reducing leakage much.

levers.lever: Family support, parenting and household programmes
levers.lever_full: Family support, parenting and household programmes that change who decides inside the home
levers.family: Exclusion from social and political spaces
levers.joins_when: it works on relations and decisions inside the household: women's control of resources, family functioning
levers.joins_not: it is about care services (L3-005) or violence (L3-007)
levers.pathways: L3-002 Gender norms and intra-household bargaining
entry_points: Family Cohesion and Home-School Relationship Strengthening
Family Capacity and Intergenerational Learning Support Programme
Promote desirable character formation in families
levers.evidence: Gender norms and intra-household bargaining: Duflo 2003; Duflo 2012; Jayachandran 2015
levers.intervention_evidence: Field, Pande, Rigol, Schaner and Troyer Moore 2021, On Her Own Account: How Strengthening Women's Financial Control Impacts Labor Supply and Gender Norms, American Economic Review
levers.evidence_finding: Paying women's public works wages into their own bank accounts, with training, raised their work and loosened restrictive gender norms in India; effects were largest where husbands had opposed women working.

levers.lever: Quotas, reserved seats and leadership programmes
levers.lever_full: Quotas, reserved seats and leadership programmes for women and excluded groups
levers.family: Exclusion from social and political spaces
levers.joins_when: it puts excluded groups into decision-making bodies or leadership
levers.joins_not: it is about attitudes in general with no decision-making role named (L3-013 or the family)
levers.pathways: L3-003 Political representation of excluded groups
entry_points: Gender equality attitudes and women’s leadership promotion
Women’s Leadership and Gender Equality Promotion Measures
levers.evidence: Political representation of excluded groups: Pande 2003; Chattopadhyay and Duflo 2004
levers.intervention_evidence: Beaman, Chattopadhyay, Duflo, Pande and Topalova 2009, Powerful Women: Does Exposure Reduce Bias?, Quarterly Journal of Economics | Beaman, Duflo, Pande and Topalova 2012, Female leadership raises aspirations and educational attainment for girls: a policy experiment in India, Science
levers.evidence_finding: Randomly reserved village council seats for women in India reduced voter bias against female leaders and raised girls' aspirations and schooling, but only after repeated exposure across two election cycles.

levers.lever: Policies that close gaps between identity groups
levers.lever_full: Policies that close gaps between identity groups: targeted services, regional equity, recognition
levers.family: Exclusion from social and political spaces
levers.joins_when: it names a gap between ethnic, religious or regional groups and acts to close it
levers.joins_not: it is about national identity (L3-014) or contact (L3-013)
levers.pathways: L3-011 Horizontal inequalities and group grievance
levers.text_cues: horizontal inequal|group grievance|grievance|between groups|ethnic (inequal|tension|minorit|group)|minority (rights|group)|indigenous|marginali[sz]ed (group|communit)|public trust|trust in (government|institution)
levers.evidence: Horizontal inequalities and group grievance: Stewart 2008; Cederman, Weidmann and Gleditsch 2011
levers.intervention_evidence: Bagde, Epple and Taylor 2016, Does Affirmative Action Work? Caste, Gender, College Quality, and Academic Success in India, American Economic Review
levers.evidence_finding: Caste reservations in Indian engineering colleges raised attendance of disadvantaged groups at better colleges without harming their academic performance; evidence on other group-targeted gap-closing policies remains limited.

levers.lever: Protection services, shelters, legal response and economic options
levers.lever_full: Protection services, shelters, legal response and economic options for women facing violence
levers.family: Violence, coercion and denial of dignity
levers.joins_when: it prevents or responds to violence against women by partners
levers.joins_not: it concerns children (L3-008, L3-009, L3-010) or crime in general (F-08)
levers.pathways: L3-007 Intimate-partner violence and women's bargaining power
levers.evidence: Intimate-partner violence and women's bargaining power: Aizer 2010
levers.intervention_evidence: Ellsberg et al. 2015, Prevention of violence against women and girls: what does the evidence say?, The Lancet | Buller et al. 2018, A Mixed-Method Review of Cash Transfers and Intimate Partner Violence in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, World Bank Research Observer
levers.evidence_finding: Cash transfers reduced partner violence in most studies, and community mobilisation and combined economic-plus-gender programmes show promise; stand-alone response services and awareness campaigns have weak evidence of preventing violence.

levers.lever: Income support and schooling that take children out of work
levers.lever_full: Income support and schooling that take children out of work; child labour enforcement
levers.family: Violence, coercion and denial of dignity
levers.joins_when: it reduces child labour or keeps children of poor households in school instead of work
levers.joins_not: it is general child protection (L3-010) or school access (L3-036)
levers.pathways: L3-008 Household poverty and child labour
levers.evidence: Household poverty and child labour: Basu and Van 1998; Edmonds 2007
levers.intervention_evidence: Dammert, de Hoop, Mvukiyehe and Rosati 2018, Effects of public policy on child labor: Current knowledge, gaps, and implications for program design, World Development
levers.evidence_finding: Cash transfers usually reduce child labour, especially when tied to schooling, but credit, asset and productive transfers can increase it by raising returns to children's work on family enterprises.

levers.lever: Laws, incentives and schooling that delay marriage
levers.lever_full: Laws, incentives and schooling that delay marriage
levers.family: Violence, coercion and denial of dignity
levers.joins_when: it raises the age of marriage or keeps girls in school to that end
levers.joins_not: it is reproductive health in general (L3-100)
levers.pathways: L3-009 Child marriage and girls' human capital
levers.evidence: Child marriage and girls' human capital: Field and Ambrus 2008
levers.intervention_evidence: Malhotra and Elnakib 2021, 20 Years of the Evidence Base on What Works to Prevent Child Marriage: A Systematic Review, Journal of Adolescent Health | Buchmann, Field, Glennerster, Nazneen and Wang 2023, A Signal to End Child Marriage: Theory and Experimental Evidence from Bangladesh, American Economic Review
levers.evidence_finding: Schooling support and conditional incentives delay marriage most consistently; a small incentive to delay marriage cut child marriage in Bangladesh, while girls' empowerment training alone did not.

levers.lever: Child protection services, case management
levers.lever_full: Child protection services, case management, early intervention after abuse or neglect
levers.family: Violence, coercion and denial of dignity
levers.joins_when: it protects children from abuse, neglect or exploitation, or treats its effects
levers.joins_not: it is early-childhood education (L3-039) or child labour (L3-008)
levers.pathways: L3-010 Early adversity and lifetime outcomes
levers.evidence: Early adversity and lifetime outcomes: Currie and Widom 2010
levers.intervention_evidence: Cluver et al. 2018, Parenting for Lifelong Health: a pragmatic cluster randomised controlled trial of a non-commercialised parenting programme for adolescents and their families in South Africa, BMJ Global Health
levers.evidence_finding: A low-cost group parenting programme reduced abuse and harsh parenting of adolescents in South Africa; evidence on child protection services and case management in low- and middle-income countries remains scarce.

levers.lever: Resettlement with livelihood restoration, compensation and housing
levers.lever_full: Resettlement with livelihood restoration, compensation and housing for the displaced
levers.joins_when: it resettles or compensates people displaced by projects, disasters or conflict
levers.joins_not: it supports voluntary migrants (L3-019) or refugees' work rights (L3-020)
levers.pathways: L3-018 Impoverishment risks of displacement
levers.evidence: Impoverishment risks of displacement: Cernea 1997
levers.intervention_evidence: Cernea and Guggenheim 1994, Resettlement and Development: The Bankwide Review of Projects Involving Involuntary Resettlement 1986-1993, World Bank Environment Department Papers
levers.evidence_finding: Review of World Bank projects found resettlers' incomes were more often not restored than restored; restoration succeeded where people were moved onto land or jobs, shared project benefits and governments were committed.

levers.lever: Support for households to move or diversify when their place cannot
levers.lever_full: Support for households to move or diversify when their place cannot sustain them
levers.joins_when: it helps people move away from environmental pressure or supports seasonal mobility
levers.joins_not: it moves assets out of hazard zones in place (L3-086) or resettles involuntarily (L3-018)
levers.pathways: L3-019 Migration as adaptation
levers.evidence: Migration as adaptation: Black et al. 2011
levers.intervention_evidence: Bryan, Chowdhury and Mobarak 2014, Underinvestment in a Profitable Technology: The Case of Seasonal Migration in Bangladesh, Econometrica
levers.evidence_finding: A small travel subsidy raised seasonal migration and household consumption during the lean season in Bangladesh; later scale-ups found smaller effects, so impacts depend on destination labour demand.

levers.lever: Work permits, services and integration programmes
levers.lever_full: Work permits, services and integration programmes for refugees and their hosts
levers.joins_when: it gives refugees or displaced foreigners access to work, services or integration
levers.joins_not: it is labour migration for earnings (F-36)
levers.pathways: L3-020 Refugee integration and host labour markets
levers.evidence: Refugee integration and host labour markets: Becker and Ferrara 2019
levers.intervention_evidence: Marbach, Hainmueller and Hangartner 2018, The long-term impact of employment bans on the economic integration of refugees, Science Advances | Clemens, Huang and Graham 2018, The Economic and Fiscal Effects of Granting Refugees Formal Labor Market Access, Center for Global Development Working Paper
levers.evidence_finding: Longer employment bans in Germany lowered refugees' employment for years afterwards; granting formal work rights tends to raise refugees' earnings and tax contributions with small effects on host workers.

levers.pathways: L3-021 Consumption smoothing through transfers and insurance; L3-022 Prevention of adverse coping; L3-023 Ex ante risk-taking under protection
levers.text_cues: unemployment (insurance|benefit)|social insurance|income support|consumption smooth|cash assistance|distress sale|coping|asset (loss|protect)|(withdraw|pull).{0,20}(children|child).{0,20}school|school withdrawal|crop insurance|agricultur(al)? insurance|index insurance|weather insurance|livestock insurance

Crop Insurance System Development
Climate Insurance Scheme Development

levers.intervention_evidence: Carter, de Janvry, Sadoulet and Sarris 2017, Index Insurance for Developing Country Agriculture: A Reassessment, Annual Review of Resource Economics | Janzen and Carter 2019, After the Drought: The Impact of Microinsurance on Consumption Smoothing and Asset Protection, American Journal of Agricultural Economics
levers.evidence_finding: Index insurance helped Kenyan herders protect assets and consumption after drought and can encourage investment, but demand at market prices is low and basis risk undermines value.

levers.lever: Registries, triggers and payment rails
levers.lever_full: Registries, triggers and payment rails that scale support automatically in a shock
levers.joins_when: it builds the system (registry, trigger, payment channel) that expands benefits fast in a crisis
levers.joins_not: it is emergency relief delivery itself (L3-244) or a transfer with no scaling mechanism (L3-021)

levers.evidence: Shock-responsive scale-up: Bowen et al. 2020
levers.intervention_evidence: Pople, Hill, Dercon and Brunckhorst 2021, Anticipatory Cash Transfers in Climate Disaster Response, CSAE Working Paper
levers.evidence_finding: Flood-forecast-triggered cash paid before peak flooding in Bangladesh improved food consumption and wellbeing more than later payments; evidence depends on accurate triggers and ready payment channels, and remains limited.

levers.lever: Pensions and old-age allowances
levers.lever_full: Pensions and old-age allowances
levers.joins_when: it provides, extends or reforms income in old age
levers.joins_not: it keeps older people working (L3-103) or provides care (L3-104)

levers.evidence_finding: Non-contributory pensions raise elderly consumption and mental health and reduce work at older ages; in South Africa pensions to women improved granddaughters' nutrition, so effects depend on who receives them.

levers.lever: Health insurance, fee exemptions and benefit packages
levers.lever_full: Health insurance, fee exemptions and benefit packages that cap what patients pay

levers.joins_not: it expands the services themselves (L3-043) or insurance for informal workers specifically (L3-260)

levers.evidence_finding: Public health insurance consistently raises use of care, but effects on out-of-pocket spending and health status are mixed, depending on benefit package depth and supply-side quality.

levers.lever: Targeting systems, poverty registries and eligibility rules
levers.lever_full: Targeting systems, poverty registries and eligibility rules
levers.joins_when: it decides or improves who receives benefits: targeting, registries, eligibility
levers.joins_not: it is the scaling mechanism in a shock (L3-024) or the data system in general (F-43)

levers.evidence_finding: Proxy-means targeting excludes many poor households but still delivers more welfare per budget than universal transfers; small application costs improved self-selection of the poor in Indonesia.

levers.lever: Unconditional cash transfers and allowances
levers.lever_full: Unconditional cash transfers and allowances
levers.joins_when: it gives cash to poor households with no condition attached
levers.joins_not: it attaches schooling or health conditions (L3-030) or bundles assets and training (L3-029)
levers.pathways: L3-028 Cash transfers and productive investment
levers.evidence: Cash transfers and productive investment: Haushofer and Shapiro 2016; Egger et al. 2022
levers.intervention_evidence: Bastagli et al. 2016, Cash transfers: what does the evidence say? A rigorous review of programme impact and of the role of design and implementation features, ODI | Pega et al. 2022, Unconditional cash transfers for reducing poverty and vulnerabilities: effect on use of health services and health outcomes in low- and middle-income countries, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
levers.evidence_finding: Unconditional transfers consistently raise consumption and reduce poverty and probably food insecurity and illness; effect size depends on transfer value, regularity and timely payment.

levers.lever: Graduation programmes
levers.lever_full: Graduation programmes: assets plus training, coaching and consumption support
levers.joins_when: it hands over productive assets with support to move households out of poverty
levers.joins_not: it is cash alone (L3-028) or microcredit (L3-173)
levers.pathways: L3-029 Big-push asset transfers
levers.text_cues: graduation (programme|program|approach)|productive asset transfer|livestock transfer|ultra-?poor|productive inclusion|livelihood package
levers.evidence: Big-push asset transfers: Banerjee et al. 2015 (Science); Bandiera et al. 2017
levers.intervention_evidence: Banerjee, Duflo and Sharma 2021, Long-Term Effects of the Targeting the Ultra Poor Program, American Economic Review: Insights | Bossuroy et al. 2022, Tackling psychosocial and capital constraints to alleviate poverty, Nature
levers.evidence_finding: Graduation programmes produced lasting gains in consumption and assets for ten years in India; in Niger, adding cash to psychosocial support raised impacts, while cheaper versions gave smaller gains.

levers.lever: Cash transfers conditioned on school attendance or health visits
levers.lever_full: Cash transfers conditioned on school attendance or health visits

levers.joins_not: it is unconditional (L3-028) or a scholarship paid by the education system (L3-040)

levers.evidence_finding: Both conditional and unconditional transfers raise enrolment and attendance; explicitly monitored and enforced conditions produce larger schooling gains, while learning effects are small.

levers.lever: Food access and food price measures
levers.lever_full: Food access measures: price support for consumers, food aid, income support in food crises; Price stabilisation and compensation for food price spikes

levers.joins_not: it is about nutrition quality (L3-054), price stabilisation on its own (L3-055) or production (F-32) (L3-053); it holds strategic food stocks (L3-205) or supports farm prices (F-33) (L3-055)

levers.evidence: Entitlement failure and food access: Sen 1981; Food price shocks and net-buyer welfare: Deaton 1989; Ivanic and Martin 2008

levers.evidence_finding: Transfers raise food consumption and dietary quality across many programmes, whereas staple price subsidies in China mostly shifted spending to other foods and did not improve calorie intake.

levers.lever: Maternal and infant nutrition programmes, breastfeeding
levers.lever_full: Maternal and infant nutrition programmes, breastfeeding, micronutrients, first-1000-days care

National Immunization Mechanism for Population Health and Child Development
National nutrition support for mothers and young children
Child nutrition support programme

levers.evidence_finding: Scaling ten proven nutrition interventions to 90 percent coverage would avert about 15 percent of child deaths; breastfeeding promotion works best when combining facility, home and community counselling.

levers.lever: Food safety standards, inspection, certification and traceability
levers.lever_full: Food safety standards, inspection, certification and traceability
levers.joins_when: it controls the safety or standards of food along the chain
levers.joins_not: it is product quality for export in general (L3-114) or animal disease (L3-163)

Food Standards Control System Strengthening
Safe Farming and Organic Certification Programme

National emergency alert and food safety traceability systems

levers.intervention_evidence: Hoffmann, Moser and Saak 2019, Food safety in low and middle-income countries: The evidence through an economic lens, World Development
levers.evidence_finding: Few rigorous evaluations show food safety regulation reducing illness in low- and middle-income countries; formal standards mainly reach export chains, while informal domestic markets need training and incentive-based approaches.

levers.lever: Storage, cold chains and post-harvest handling
levers.lever_full: Storage, cold chains and post-harvest handling
levers.joins_when: it cuts losses between harvest and market: storage, handling, cold chain
levers.joins_not: it is transport to market (L3-155) or processing industry (L3-151)

levers.evidence_finding: Hermetic storage bags cut losses and lean-season food insecurity in Uganda, and harvest-time credit let Kenyan farmers store and sell later at higher prices, though gains shrink when many farmers store.

levers.evidence_finding: School feeding modestly raises enrolment, attendance and some learning and anthropometric outcomes, with stronger effects in food-insecure settings and where meals are regular and of adequate quality.

levers.lever: Policing, sanctions and their certainty

levers.evidence_finding: Policing focused on crime hot spots reduces crime with little displacement, but multi-country trials of community policing in the Global South found no gains in crime or trust.

levers.lever_full: Prevention programmes for at-risk people: therapy, mentoring, drug demand reduction, community engagement

levers.evidence_finding: Short cognitive behavioural therapy for high-risk men in Liberia cut crime and violence for a decade, and focused deterrence and therapy-based programmes outperform broad, untargeted prevention.

levers.evidence_finding: A judicial reform that sped up case resolution in Pakistan raised contract enforcement and small-firm investment; rigorous evidence on legal aid and alternative dispute resolution for the poor remains scarce.

levers.evidence_finding: Electronic monitoring instead of prison cut reoffending in Argentina, and cognitive behavioural programmes reduce recidivism by about a quarter, especially for higher-risk offenders and well-implemented programmes.

levers.lever: Enforcement against trafficking, drug markets and organised crime

levers.evidence_finding: Most studies find intensified drug enforcement increases market violence, and supply shortages raised homicides in Mexico; crackdowns reduce violence only when paired with institutions able to absorb displaced trade.

levers.evidence_finding: Grid connections bring gains in lighting, study time and home business, but effects on incomes are often small where consumption is low and complementary inputs or reliable supply are lacking.

levers.evidence_finding: Water treatment and piped water reduce child diarrhoea and mortality substantially, while basic sanitation shows weaker effects; gains depend on sustained use and high community-wide coverage.

levers.lever: Clean cooking fuels and stoves

levers.evidence_finding: Free LPG stoves and fuel did not improve birth weight in a four-country trial, while efficient charcoal stoves in Kenya cut fuel spending; health gains require near-exclusive clean fuel use.

levers.evidence_finding: Slum upgrading evidence is limited but suggests health gains from water and floor improvements; relocation to formal housing in India broke social networks and many winners moved back.

levers.evidence_finding: Expanding primary care teams in Brazil and access to local providers in Thailand reduced infant mortality, with gains concentrated in poorer areas where facilities were added and staffed.

levers.evidence_finding: Combining training with supervision or group problem solving improves provider practice more than training or guidelines alone; performance pay in Rwanda raised institutional deliveries and service quality.
